title: Attention kernel choice predictor and safeguarded rollout
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Problem: FlashAttention v3 and other new attention kernels sometimes improve median latency but increase p95 for a subset of short or highly-quantized requests. We need a lightweight per-request kernel chooser that predicts the lowest-cost, stable kernel for the incoming request characteristics and falls back safely to conservative kernels when risk is detected. Goal: reduce p95 regressions during v3 rollout and enable quick rollback-free mitigation with minimal overhead.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Deployed predictor that selects kernel per-request with <=0.6ms added tail latency for selection path and improves observed p95 by >=8% on canary traffic compared to naive v3-only routing. 2) Feature extraction cost tested across CPU/GPU hosts and bounded. 3) Canary config in Console with automated rollback if p95 increase >5% for 5m window. 4) End-to-end tests and canary dashboard links present. 5) Documentation for ops and runbook updated.
design_notes: Approach: build a compact gradient-boosted tree (GBDT) predictor using offline traces. Features: request sequence length, batch size, effective QKV dtype (fp16/int8/4-bit), token distribution (leading pad %, average token entropy proxy), model family tag, prefix cache hit boolean, and observed workspace pressure estimate from recent allocator stats. Keep model < 100KB serialized and do inference in-process (C++ shim) to avoid RPCs. Fallback policy: if predictor confidence < threshold OR workspace_pressure high OR telemetry indicates increase in error rate, route to conservative kernel (FlashAttn-v2-like path).
implementation_plan: 1) Data collection: instrument runtime to log features and per-kernel latency/p95 for a 2-week window (sampled 1/100). 2) Offline training pipeline in an internal notebook (scikit/xgboost) and small hyperparameter sweep. 3) Export model to ONNX/treelite minimal runtime and embed in C++ runtime; add feature extractor. 4) End-to-end harness + microbench to measure selection overhead. 5) Canary in production: 1% traffic, monitor p50/p95, error rate, OOMs. 6) Gradually increase to 20% then 50% with rollback gates. 7) Postmortem and iterate on features/thresholds.

tradeoffs_and_risks:
- Risk: Feature extractor CPU overhead may increase host contention under extreme load; mitigation: offload to a pinned selection thread and throttle sampling.
- Risk: Model overfits to sampled traffic segments leading to oscillation; mitigation: periodic retrain and use conservative smoothing + confidence threshold.
- Tradeoff: More features improve accuracy but increase inference cost and surface area; we prioritize small set of high-signal features.
- Failure mode: Predictor misroutes causing p95 regressions; safeguard by immediate rollback threshold and per-route circuit breaker in Console.
canary_strategy_and_gates:
Phase 0: internal staging tests against synthetic traces.
Phase 1: 1% production traffic for 24h; observe p50/p95, error-rate, and OOM frequency.
Gate: abort if p95 worsens by >5% or errors+OOMs increase by >2x.
Phase 2: 10% for 48h; Gate: abort if p95 worsens by >3% or sustained CPU pressure on selection thread observed.
Phase 3: 50% then full rollout with 1h observation windows. All canaries instrumented with automated alarms in PagerDuty.
testing_and_validation:
- Unit tests for feature extractor and deterministic model runner.
- Microbench suites for overhead (latency + CPU) across instance families.
- End-to-end regression tests with synthetic workloads (short/long sequences, mixed dtypes).
- Backtest against previous 30 days of traces to estimate p95 delta.
- Chaos test where fallback path is forced to validate rollback correctness.

postmortem_plan: If a regression occurs during canary or rollout, collect deterministic trace (via request id sampling), revert selector to config-route->conservative-kernel, and open incident doc. Post-incident analysis will include feature attribution, retrain with augmented dataset, and adjust confidence thresholds.
